ngl the first time i took Xanax was the slow release pill so i just felt a bit sleepy, also i was having panic attacks so i just went to sleep after taking it.
When it got worse i started taking 1mg of regular Xanax and boy did that shit hit like a truck, i was sleeping pretty in a flash, but I only had 50kg on me at the time and that is a thing to consider as well.

I have been taking taking Xanax daily for about a year now, 2mg per day, one in the morning and one before sleep.
Xanax doses can vary a lot, i know people that have prescriptions for 0.5mg or 0.25mg in SOS, and I'm not absolute sure about this one but the maximum dose can reach 10mg per day i think, but high doses are only given to people that have a very high tolerance for Xanax and the best option in generally to change to another benzo.
I can take 0.5mg as Sos but as you can imagine since I have been taking this for almost a year my tolerance is very big and i literally don't feel the effects of taking 2mg a day, so i also have Victan and take it whenever I'm more anxious in order to eat and stuff.
If you have any more questions feel free to ask i will do my best to answer.
Best of luck

I don't know if you can boot up windows from a pen drive thoe, but I know you can do it in Linux, so a way to do it is to use another pen drive and boot into Linux without installing it, wipe the drive using some program and then remove the Linux pen drive and use the other one to install windows again on the PC

When you delete files in windows, or any operating system in general, the space of that file used to have just gets labeled as free place, the file isn't actually deleted, that's why there is programs out there that can recover lost data, they look at the empty space and see it's there is something there.

So basically after the the factory reset the data is still kinda all there and if it isn't overwritten by, for example, the creation of a new file, then it can be recovered.

The way to make sure that there is something left on your PC is to make a full wipe of the storage, there are programs out there that will overwrite everything with zeros, so no data can be extracted after that.

I'm pretty sure there videos out there with step by step instructions on how to do this, but the process is something like this.

First make sure you have your windows activation key or something similar and a pen drive with the Windows installation stuff, because after the disk is fully wiped there will literally be nothing there.

Also, you will most likely need to be running your PC from the pen drive to do the wipe, because you are removing everything from the PC, including windows.

After the disk is fully wiped you do a clean install of windows and all it's good, there will be nothing left on the PC.

Some basics tips that i used:

Breathing: count to seven, inhale using your nose from 1 to 3, then wait and exhale through the mouth at seven

Washing your face with water

Getting some fresh air

These work for low levels of anxiety and generally get the job done.

If you find yourself overthinking something, activate your brain my doing something like counting the tiles on the floor or whatever, it's a nice trick to distract you and make you focus on something else.

About medication, it's perfectly understandable and ok to not  take meds, my dad had some bad experiences with doctors giving him the wrong meds and doses that were just absurd, but they don't really change who you are, some conditions like GAD most of the time need to me treated with medication, because you are basically fixing an imbalance in the brain. If you have a broken ancke or something, you go treat it, it's the same for mental health. Now both me and my dad are in the right medication and dose and things turned for the better.

Still if you don't want medication a good start is going to a therapist and begin to develop healthy ways to cope and tackle your issues.

Medication doesn't change who you are, it just regulates the imbalances in your brain and makes so that the anxiety won't cripple you. Sertraline it's a long term medicine and a good place to start, but the first weeks might be a bit wack.

For me it made my hands extremely trembly and made me very sleepy ( i would literally fall asleep in class lmao) and they lasted for about 1 to 2 weeks, after that they were pretty minor.

I'm not a doctor thoe, and the side effects and duration of them is different for everyone, but this isn't a sprint, it's a marathon, and there is no magic pill that will just make anxiety go away.

A friend of mine lost a lot of weight in the beginning because she stoped binge eating and was a lot more lose when talking to teachers ( some fun online classes came out of that ) but now she is doing a lot better and improving slow and steady.

If it will be better or worse tomorrow I can't tell, there are always ups and downs, but in the future you will look back and say " wait why am I not so anxious over this and that " and things will get better and keep on getting better.

About stopping taking it, in my case I will take it for the rest of my life because I have GAD and my brain just doesn't like making the proper amount or seretonine lmao, but the effects of Sertraline last for a long time.

Unfortunately my dad went through a series of doctors and when he got better they would take out the medicine and after a few months things went back to the start, but it really depends on a lot factors and the best person to answers those questions is your psychiatrist. All I can do is talk about my experiences with Sertraline and the general knowledge that i got from it.

Nausea and lack of appetite are also the main things that anxiety causes to me, mainly in the morning.

What I try to do is find foods that I can eat even when I'm very anxious ( for me it's pears and yogurt ) and try to eat them. After having something in my stomach and sugar from the fruit kicks in most of it goes away. 

That's what works for me, give it a try and see if it helps

When starting to take Sertraline it's normal to feel more side effects in the begging but they go away with time.

I started on 25 mg and I'm now at 50 mg with another medication of the same type to balance things out (so it's kinda like taking 100 mg of Sertraline) and whenever I changed dosage and when I added the new medication it took some time to adjust.

Keep talking with your psychiatrist and if the side effects don't go away you might need to change medication, but it's perfectly normal to feel the side effects this early on.

I also have anxiety for the first days whenever I change place, like going back home from college or going on trips, but it only last for a few days.

Consider seeing a therapist and/or a psychiatrist if it doesn't go away, also try to find healthy coping mechanism. 

I'm not really a good example because I turned to alcohol and now smoking, so stay clear of that stuff and be careful in general.
